text:
incident-bot: ALERT — p99 latency > 1.2s for route /v1/generate in prod (us-east-1). current window: 3m. SLO p99=1.0s. graph: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rtg/prod-latency?panel=7 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident P-87234 fired (High) — impacted service: inference-api-prod. Escalation: @Sam L -> oncall.
Sam L: acked. pulling up dashboard now. I’m on 🔍
Alex R: seeing p95 ~380ms -> jumped from 90ms. p99 ~1.35s. qps steady. no 5xx spike in the last 2m.
Mira: looking at kvcache evictions — eviction rate spiked ~1719902050. logs: `kvcache: evict keys=12, compaction=1, latency_ms=4` then CPU on sidecars climbed. possible KV hotkey?
Jonah: hitting autoscaler — scale decision delayed; noticed cooldown was set to 300s. going to manually scale hot path pool to relieve tail.
Jonah: running: ```kubectl scale deployment redwood-inference-hotpath --replicas=12 -n prod```. output: `deployment.apps/redwood-inference-hotpath scaled`
ops-bot: Scaling event: redwood-inference-hotpath -> 12 replicas (triggered by Jonah).
Alex R: after scale start, p99 still ~1.2s (warmup). can we fallback to smaller model for high QPS routes? fallback policy exists for model-3 -> model-3-sm quantized.
Sam L: go for fallback as test. Mira please confirm compatibility with structured outputs.
Mira: model-3-sm supports current handler but tokenization differs slightly; quality delta should be low for ephemeral fallbacks. running a quick canary: ```curl -s -X POST https://prod-api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"model-3-sm","prompt":"hello"}' | jq '.latency_ms'```
Mira: canary shows latency 120ms, responses look okay on quick checks.
Sam L: ok enable fallback route: `route policy set /v1/generate fallback=model-3-sm if p99>1.0s` — implementing now.
Jonah: traffic rerouted. confirming autoscaler reports added capacity and that sidecars warmed caches.
Alex R: p99 dropped to ~0.88s within 2m of fallback + scale. p95 back to ~110ms.
incident-bot: PagerDuty P-87234 acknowledged by Sam L at 1719902178.
Sam L: notes: no increase in 5xx. customer-visible errors: none reported yet. severity: high SLO burn but limited user impact so far.
Mira: digging deeper — KV eviction correlates with a batch job running every 5m that spikes mem usage on a subset of nodes. filtering logs: `cron:shard-maintenance job=kv-compact shard=7 mem_mb=6100` while node memory is 8GB. that likely caused eviction ripple.
Alex R: can we throttle that cron? if it runs during peak, it's bad. who owns shard-maintenance?
Mira: ops-libs team runs that. pinging @Jonah to put a temporary schedule change.
Jonah: messaged ops-libs in #eng-ops, they agree to pause the maintenance window for 15m. applied `kubectl annotate cronjob/kv-compact paused=true -n infra`.
ops-bot: Cronjob kv-compact annotated paused=true by Jonah.
Sam L: good mitigation. plan: 1) pause cron, 2) keep autoscaled pool until no regression for 30m, 3) follow-up: lower autoscaler cooldown to 90s and add alert for kv-compact overlap. assign follow-ups.
Alex R: agree. logging ticket: #INF-4297 to track runbook changes and alert tuning.
Mira: leaving additional note — add eviction metric to the route SLO dashboard so triage surfaces this earlier.
Sam L: thanks. monitoring: p99 stable ~0.85s for last 5m. no new PD pages.
pagerduty: PagerDuty P-87234 status -> acknowledged -> resolved (manual) at 1719903299.
Sam L: closing thread in 10m if stable. will take ownership of postmortem. action items: @Jonah adjust autoscaler cooldown, @Mira dashboard change, @Alex confirm no hidden customer impact.
Jonah: autoscaler cooldown lowered to 90s in prod (change-id: ch-9832).
Alex R: verified no user-facing errors in the API logs for the window 1719901800-1719903300. sampling request IDs show successful responses.
Sam L: summary for postmortem: root cause: maintenance job overlapped peak causing KV evictions -> cache misses -> increased p99. mitigations: pause job, scale pool, enable fallback model, tune autoscaler cooldown, add alerting. ETA for follow-up doc: EOD.
Mira: also recommend making cron job obey cluster load window (API CPU/p95) before running. will draft RFC.
Sam L: thanks all — reassigning incident P-87234 -> postmortem owner Sam L. ops handled, resolved, monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
